stories.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Manusmriti Remark Sparks BJP-Congress War Over Women’s Rights

Speaking at Congress’s youth outreach programme in Pune, Rahul Gandhi criticised the Manusmriti’s traditional prescriptions on women and accused the BJP and RSS of promoting a “Manusmriti mindset”. He urged young women to “smash patriarchy” and asserted that women are individuals, not property. The BJP has hit back, accusing Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over women’s representation and questioning his stance on the Women’s Reservation Bill. BJP leader Smriti Irani also pointed to the absence of women ministers in the Congress-led Karnataka cabinet. What began as Rahul’s call to challenge patriarchy has now turned into another sharp Congress-BJP political face-off.

stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 3.5 strikes Leh
stories.summary: Leh , August 24 : An earthquake of magnitude 3.5 struck Ladakh's capital, Leh, early Monday morning, reported the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). Sharing details in a post on X, the seismic monitoring agency stated that the tremor occurred at a depth of 120 km at 8:25 AM Indian Standard Time (IST). "EQ of M: 3.5, On: 24/08/2026 08:25:07 IST, Lat: 36.700 N, Long: 74.343 E, Depth: 120 Km, Location: Leh, Ladakh," the post read. Hours before the Leh earthquake, Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district was also hit by a mild earthquake of magnitude 3.0 at 3:40 AM on Monday. Providing details about the Chamba quake, the NCS posted, "EQ of M: 3.0, On: 24/08/2026 03:40:19 IST, Lat: 32.925 N, Long: 76.145 E, Depth: 8 Km, Location: Chamba, Himachal Pradesh." Earlier, an earthquake measuring 4.6 on the Richter scale struck the Leh region on Sunday. According to the NCS, Sunday's tremor was recorded at a depth of 150 km at 3:34 PM IST. "EQ of M: 4.6, On: 23/08/2026 15:34:42 IST, Lat: 36.736 N, Long: 74.372 E, Depth: 150 Km, Location: Leh Ladakh, Ladakh," the post read. (ANI)

article_sentences: New Delhi: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah will attend the 9th National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference, scheduled to be held in New Delhi on August 24 and 25.
The conference will be conducted in a hybrid format, with participants attending both physically and virtually.

More than 850 officers from various security and police forces across the country are expected to deliberate on contemporary issues and emerging challenges related to national security during the two-day conference.
Last year, the two-day 8th National Security Strategies (NSS) Conference-2025 was inaugurated by Shah in New Delhi and was held in a hybrid format, combining physical and virtual modes.
As per the release, around 800 officers participated from across the country and deliberated on various subjects related to national security.
Among senior officers, the Union Home Secretary, Deputy NSA and Heads of CAPFs and CPOs attended the Conference in Delhi.

The DGsP of States and UTs, as well as young police officers at the cutting-edge level and domain experts from specialised fields, joined the Conference from the respective state capitals through the virtual mode.

The first day of the Conference focused on the role of external actors who are inimical to the interests of the nation and their domestic linkages, including involvement in the narcotics trade; challenges posed by illegal use of encrypted communication apps and other latest technologies; and use of technology for crowd management and security of uninhabited islands.
The issues related to financing of terror were also deliberated.
The second day of the Conference would focus on civil aviation and port security, counter terrorism, Left Wing Extremism and countermeasures for Narcotics trafficking.

stories.title: Supreme Court Restores Congress Leaders Petition Challenging BJP MP's Election From Assam

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (August 24) restored an election petition filed by advocate and Indian National Congress member Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury, challenging the election of Bharatiya Janata Party's Kripanath Mallah, who won the Lok Sabha elections from the No. 7 Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency in Assam during the 2024 General Elections.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran allowed the civil appeal, which has been preferred under Section 116A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, challenging the Gauhati High Court's judgment dated April 4, 2025, which rejected the election petition at the threshold.

By the said judgment, the High Court had dismissed the election petition filed by Choudhary challenging the election of Kripanath, alleging corrupt practices within the meaning of Section 123 of the RP Act.

However, the returned candidate filed an application under Section 86, read with Sections 81 and 83 of the RoP Act, and Section 151 CPC, seeking the outright dismissal of the election petition at the threshold, without going into a full trial.
This was allowed by the High Court.
Choudhury had contested the 2024 parliamentary election from the Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency.
As recorded in the appeal papers, the appellant had secured 5,26,733 votes, while the returned candidate had secured 5,45,093 votes, the difference being 18,360 votes.
Justice Chandran pronounced the judgment as: "Relying on the earlier Constitution Bench judgment, we have allowed the appeal."
Detailed judgment awaited.

article_sentences: The High Court extended its interim order restraining the Election Commission from notifying the bypolls until September 8.
It also declined the TVK government's request to vacate the stay.
The Election Commission of India has told the Madras High Court that it will not notify bye-elections to five vacant Tamil Nadu Assembly seats until petitions challenging their results are decided.
The seats are Tiruchi East, Perundurai, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai and Karur.
Tiruchi East was represented by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, while the other four were held by the AIADMK.
Tamil Nadu Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik made the submission in response to a petition filed by Tirunelveli resident K Venkatachalapathy.

Venkatachalapathy has argued that the seats cannot be treated as “clear vacancies” under Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, while election petitions concerning them remain pending.
Vijay and four AIADMK candidates were elected from the five constituencies in May 2026 but later resigned.
The four former AIADMK MLAs subsequently joined Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).
Chief Minister Vijay contested and won from two Assembly constituencies, Perambur and Tiruchi East.
He retained Perambur and resigned from Tiruchi East.
S Jeyakumar, Esakki Subaya, C Vijayabaskar and MR Vijayabhaskar were elected from Perundurai, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai and Karur, respectively.

stories.headline: One Nation One Election monstrous, unconstitutional: Chidambaram to parl panel
stories.title: One Nation One Election monstrous, unconstitutional: Chidambaram to parl panel
stories.summary: One Nation One Election monstrous, unconstitutional: Chidambaram to parl panel
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Former Union Minister P Chidambaram opposed the "One Nation, One Election" proposal before a parliamentary panel, calling it "monstrous", "unconstitutional" and "mindless".
He argued that curtailing legislatures' five-year terms violates the Constitution's basic structure.
TMC's Sagarika Ghosh also opposed the bills, while Padma awardees remained divided over simultaneous polls.

Former Union Minister P Chidambaram on Monday strongly opposed the move to hold simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies before a joint committee of Parliament, terming the initiative "monstrous" and "unconstitutional."
The former home and finance minister also said that the proposal to hold nationwide polls under "One Nation, One Election" is a "mindless" exercise.

Sources said Chidambaram submitted his opinion while appearing before the joint committee of Parliament on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which aim to synchronise Lok Sabha and state assembly polls.

The Congress leader submitted that the bills on simultaneous polls are "unconstitutional." He argued that since any legislature is elected for a five-year term, curtailing its tenure directly violates the basic structure of the Constitution, sources aware of the deliberations said.

The senior Congress leader also said that his conscience does not allow him to support the bills and stressed that the government does not have the number (two-thirds majority) to pass the legislation, sources said.
TMC's Sagarika Ghosh, a member of the panel, also opposed the bill and said it would give "unbridled" power to the Election Commission.
A group of about 10 Padma awardees, including Tarlochan Singh, Navin Khanna, Meenakshi Jain and Niru Kumar, also appeared separately before the panel headed by BJP member PP Chaudhary.
While some of the Padma awardees supported the initiative of simultaneous polls, others opposed it, saying it may bring "chaos" in the country.
The bills were introduced in Lok Sabha in December 2024, following which they were referred to the joint committee for examination.

stories.headline: MNRE Offers Force Majeure Relief to Renewable Projects Hit by West Asia Crisis
stories.title: MNRE Offers Force Majeure Relief to Renewable Projects Hit by West Asia Crisis
stories.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has recently issued an advisory to grant a time extension to renewable energy projects affected by Force Majeure. It advised Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) and States/UTs after receiving various representations seeking a time extension and other reliefs due to the ongoing West Asia crisis. The advisory is granted in line with the provisions and procedures for seeking relief under the Force Majeure provisions in the PPA. They granted this extension to projects whose SCSD/SCD or extended SCSD/SCD falls on or after February 28, 2026, for a period of up to four months. MNRE's latest advisory extends to Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs), namely Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited ( SEC I), NTPC Limited, NHPC Limited and SJVN Limited, as well as Power/Energy/Renewable Energy Departments of State/UT Governments and organisations/agencies thereunder. I n line with the provision, the Ministry has notified that Force Majeure provisions in the Power Purchase Agreements ( PPAs ) and as per the contractual provisions and procedure, the REIAs/the concerned RE power procuring agencies/entities may consider granting a time extension in the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date (SCSD)/Scheduled Commissioning Date (SCD) for such renewable energy (RE) power projects. Background Initially, MNRE received representations regarding the issue based on the rising West Asia crisis and issued notices on April 29, 2026, and later on July 6, 2026. In the recent request, developers had sought a time extension for the implementation of their renewable power projects, citing delays in implementation due to disruptions caused by the situation in West Asia. Subsequently, after receiving representations, MNRE also received a request seeking a blanket extension of project timelines for affected renewable energy projects, citing an advisory issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). The issue was further taken up on April 29, 2026, by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, with the regulatory authorities indicating that an advisory should be issued. In response to this, the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, clarified that the West Asia situation should be treated as a war and provided for a time extension of up to four months on account of the West Asia situation.

stories.title: Supreme Court bans construction within 100 metres of Jojari River in Rajasthan
stories.summary: This is the latest in a series of orders passed by the Supreme Court to protect the seasonal river, which has faced a barrage of contamination that has affected around two million lives in the water-starved State.

article_sentences: A Supreme Court Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta has banned any construction or development within 100 metres of Jojari River in Rajasthan,hearing a suo motu case on Monday (August 24, 2026).
The court also prohibited hazardous industries within 500 metres of the river’s flow path.

This is the latest in a series of orders passed by the court to protect the seasonal river, which has faced a barrage of contamination that has affected around two million lives in the water-starved State.
The Supreme Court on August 4, suggested that the Rajasthan government prepare a 20-point resolution plan to deal with the issue of contamination in the Jojari, Bandi and Luni rivers in the State.
The Jojari river passes through Jodhpur, the Bandi river flows through Pali, and the Luni river runs through Balotra.
The Bandi and Jojari rivers merge with the Luni river near Balotra city.

The Supreme Court said that the entire industrial area in Pali is located along the river bank and in the long run, the State authorities may have to consider relocating industries away from the river.
“Let the State come out with a resolution plan,” it said.

stories.headline: The Growing Complexity of Renewable Energy Insurance: Managing Risks in India's Clean Energy
stories.title: The Growing Complexity of Renewable Energy Insurance: Managing Risks in India's Clean Energy
stories.summary: India's journey towards renewable energy has entered a pivotal phase, where addressing risks has become crucial. By June 2026, the nation had achieved an impressive 288.6 GW of renewable capacity, with solar contributing 162.2 GW and wind 57.4 GW. This milestone not only surpasses its goal of 50% non-fossil power by 2030 but also highlights the country's commitment to a sustainable future, as reported by the Ministry of New and Renewable However, a report from Zurich Resilience Solutions in July 2026 raised some alarms. It indicated that 90% of planned renewable projects across 871 sites might face significant climate risks by 2030 The encouraging part is that with targeted resilience measures, these potential climate-related losses could drop from $55 billion to $27 billion. This is a critical juncture for India to bolster its renewable energy initiatives and ensure they are robust against looming challenges. The insurance landscape is evolving as well. It is no longer just about safeguarding solar panels, wind turbines, or construction equipment from physical damage. As renewable projects expand in size and become more interconnected, they are increasingly vulnerable to climate events. A single cyclone, flood, or hailstorm can impact numerous assets, contractors, and transmission links in the same region, creating accumulation risks for insurers and potentially amplifying losses for developers. This evolving risk scenario is significant because renewable infrastructure is built around delicate project economics. A lengthy outage is not simply a matter of repair costs; it can lead to lost energy generation, delayed debt repayments, and renegotiated contracts. Thus, the conversation around insurance needs to transition from merely protecting assets to safeguarding the very economics of these projects. “Climate exposure starts before construction.” It is vital to recognise that climate exposure can begin long before construction starts. The most impactful insurance decisions are often made before securing a policy. Site selection, drainage design, equipment elevation, and even fire protection plays critical roles in shaping a project's risk profile. The recent Zurich assessment underscores that resilience can substantially alter how climate risks are viewed economically. For developers, this means integrating climate risk analysis into the early stages of engineering and financing. For brokers, it requires ensuring that risk information reaches underwriters in a way that mirrors the actual design and operating environment of each project. Improved information flow can differentiate between risks that are broadly imprecise and those that are well-understood. “New technologies are creating new underwriting questions .” India's renewable energy landscape is becoming more technology-driven, introducing new underwriting challenges. As battery energy storage systems gain importance alongside solar and wind resources, they also bring forth risks that traditional power policies were not designed to cover. Issues like thermal events, system integration failures, and long-term performance concerns necessitate more specialized underwriting approaches. Additionally, the rise of digital monitoring and remote controls adds layers of complexity, exposing assets to cyber risks in an industry historically focused on physical challenges. As a result, insurers cannot depend solely on historical claims data when many of the technologies currently deployed are new. Underwriting will increasingly hinge on engineering data, technology standards, operating procedures, and the quality of risk management. “Insurance must become part of project architecture.” To support India’s clean energy ambitions, insurance needs to evolve beyond a mere financial requirement to a form of risk intelligence. Brokers play a crucial role in this transformation, needing to distil intricate engineering and climate data into insurance structures that work financially, while also helping developers identify opportunities to mitigate risks rather than exclusively transferring them. This shift opens avenues for more advanced solutions, including coverage linked to business interruption, performance, and, where applicable, measurable weather triggers. Such products should enhance, not replace, sound project design. The goal is not to provide insurance for inadequate infrastructure but to make resilience a visible and economically viable priority. “The next phase will reward resilience .” As we reflect on India’s renewable energy achievements, we should focus not only on the gigawatts of capacity added or investments mobilised but also on how reliably that capacity can operate under increasingly volatile conditions. Achieving this requires a closer collaboration among developers, lenders, engineers, insurers, and brokers, ensuring that risk management is as pivotal as technology, costs, and returns.

stories.headline: Power hike a compulsion, never promised rate won’t increase: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.title: Power hike a compulsion, never promised rate won’t increase: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 24: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday said there was no crisis in the government and maintained that any cabinet reshuffle would be carried out when he deemed it necessary, while defending the recent electricity tariff hike and calling for a thorough investigation into fresh threats to Kashmiri Pandit employees. “There is no crisis in the government. Our work is going on,” Abdullah said when asked about a possible reshuffle in his government. He said he had only ruled out a reshuffle before August 15 when asked about it earlier, and had not committed to carrying it out immediately afterwards. “I only told you that it would not happen before August 15. When it will happen and under what circumstances, leave that to me,” he said. On criticism from opposition parties over the increase in electricity tariffs, Abdullah said his government had never promised that power rates would not rise. He reiterated that the government’s commitment was to provide 200 units of free electricity to the poorest households. “I repeatedly explained in the Assembly that under the free electricity scheme, we would use solar panels to deliver this benefit to people,” he said. Abdullah argued that the tariff increase was separate from the free-power scheme and said the government had raised rates by only 6 per cent after four years. “We are not celebrating the increase in electricity rates. It was a compulsion for us,” he said, adding that lower power-sector losses would reduce the need for such measures in the future. On fresh threats reportedly targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees, Abdullah described the issue as a serious concern and urged the police and intelligence agencies to investigate their source. “Threats should not be coming at all,” he said, adding that the law-and-order and security agencies “should not take these things lightly”. He recalled that Pandit employees had been targeted under similar circumstances two to two-and-a-half years ago, saying the government had suffered “a great deal of loss” as a result. “Keeping all our employees safe and protecting them is a very major responsibility of the police,” Abdullah said. He also clarified that law and order was not his direct responsibility, saying the matter was handled by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha. “My advice to the law-and-order administration would be not to take this lightly. There should be a full investigation,” he said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(August 24) said that it will pass orders on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal's application for exemption from surrendering after the Bombay High Court convicted and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment in the 2013 rape case.
The matter was heard by a single judge, Justice Alok Aradhe.

At the outset, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta(for the State of Goa) argued that the special leave petition is not admissible since the convict has not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013.

Mehta, relying on the Supreme Court judgments, stated that where the appeal has been filed, it shall state whether the convict has surrendered or not, and where he has not surrendered, the appeal should not be accepted unless accompanied by an exemption application from surrendering.
Countering this, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal(for Tejpal) said the rule doesn't apply to his case as the High Court already granted him four weeks to surrender.
After brief arguments, the Court orally stated that it will pass orders.
This comes days after the Goa Government also approached the Supreme Court for enhancement of punishment to life imprisonment while not challenging the finding of conviction.
The Bombay High Court's Goa bench, comprising Justices Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar, had on August 6 overturned Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court and convicted him in the 2013 case.
The court subsequently sentenced him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.
The High Court had noted that the incident took place 13 years ago and that there was no report of any subsequent criminal misconduct by Tejpal.
It consequently declined the Goa government's request for the maximum punishment of life imprisonment and imposed the minimum sentence prescribed for the rape conviction.
The case arose from allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside an elevator at a luxury hotel in Goa during an event organised by Tehelka in November 2013.

stories.title: Supreme Court To Consider If Co-opting Ex-HC Judges As Women Bar Council Members Attracts Article 220 Restriction
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday said that it will consider whether co-opting former High Court Judges as women members in State Bar Councils will attract the bar under Article 220 of the Constitution, which prohibits a former High Court Judge from practising in that Court.
A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant heard the arguments raised by Senior Advocate Sanjay Parikh against the inclusion of a former High Court Judge.
Making an oral mention, Parikh, who was representing six Councils, submitted that the Supreme Court did not consider many aspects, such as the Dhulia committee reports, before passing the order.
Parikh asked if the Court can pass an order invoking Article 142 of the Constitution contrary to the Advocates Act.
The CJI replied that the Court was constrained to pass such an order as there were recurring repeated applications by various parties regarding the manner of implementing co-option.
"Every day there was a new application, new mentioning.
Every day new criteria was suggested and it was becoming very difficult," the CJI pointed out.
The CJI underscored that it was passed to ensure women's representation, which everyone welcomed.
Parikh, however submitted that a Constitutional issue could arise because, as per Article 220 of the Constitution, a retired High Court Judge cannot practice in the same Court.
Therefore, if a retired High Court Judge is made a member of the Bar Council, it could attract the bar under Article 220.
"The jurisdictional judge cannot practice.
So therefore, if a person who is barred from practice is made a member of the Advocates' body...," Parikh submitted.

The Supreme Court today(August 24) directed the State of Kerala to file a counter-affidavit in a writ petition filed by Muhammed Ameer Ul Islam seeking transfer from prison in Kerala to a prison in his home State of Assam.
Islam, a migrant labourer from Assam, was convicted and sentenced to death in the 2016 Perumbavoor law student rape and murder case.

During the hearing, the bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu questioned the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services (Management) Rules, 2010, which disallow transfer of death convicts from one prison to another State contrary to the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950.
The bench asked the State of Kerala to consider amending the Rule.

Senior Advocate Rebecca John(for Islam) read Section 3 of the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950, and stated that prisoners sentenced to death are not allowed to be transferred unless the proceedings before the Trial Court and the High Court are over.
Referring to this, she pointed out that the Trial Court has already sentenced him to death, which was confirmed by the Kerala High Court in 2024.
On this, Justice Datta asked: "Where is the consent of Assam?"
John responded that the consent of the State of Assam is yet to come.
"Consent of Assam would come, but there is an outright refusal of Kerala.
Assam is saying we will consider if only Kerala allows," John said.

Referring to the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services (Management) Rules, Justice Datta asked if the petitioner has challenged Rule 587, which says that those sentenced to death are restricted from being transferred to prisons in other States.

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the State of Jharkhand and the Jharkhand Public Service Commission on a writ petition seeking an independent, time-bound investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation(CBI) into the alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition filed by activist Harisharan Devgan.
Senior Advocate Manan Kumar Misha, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the students have been protesting for over a month against the exam malpractices.
Though the State cancelled the exams, the High Court immediately stayed the decision, with the State "indirectly" supporting the challenge, Mishra contended.
Mishra submitted that the investigation be either handed over to the CBI or to a retired Supreme Court Judge.
CJI Surya Kant replied that a former Judge cannot be asked to handle the investigation.

The petition, filed through Advocate Satyam Singh Rajput, has sought the transfer of the investigation from the State to the CBI to ensure an impartial probe into the public officials and examination agencies.
The probe has been sought in light of the plea that the State's cancellation of the examination doesn't eliminate the need to uncover the "systematic corruption".
Other prayers sought are that the physical and digital evidence must be secured, including original and candidate-held OMR carbon copies, CCTV footage, and server audit logs, to prevent tampering.

stories.headline: As Doval arrives in Beijing, Cong questions shift from border resolution to management
stories.title: As Doval arrives in Beijing, Cong questions shift from border resolution to management
stories.summary: The Congress on Monday questioned the Centre’s handling of the India-China boundary dispute as National Security Advisor Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing for the latest round of talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
article_sentences: The Congress on Monday questioned the Centre’s handling of the India-China boundary dispute as National Security Advisor Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing for the latest round of talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.
Doval and Wang, their countries designated Special Representatives on the boundary question, will hold the 25th round of talks on Tuesday.
The mechanism was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the dispute along the 3,488-km India-China border.

Congress spokesperson and MP Pawan Khera said the mechanism, created during former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure, had gradually shifted from resolving the dispute to merely managing it.
“The Special Representative mechanism created during Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure was meant for border resolution.
Notice the word carefully: ‘resolution’.
But over time, it has been reduced to border management — not solving the dispute, but merely managing it,” Khera said.
He also criticised the government’s handling of the 2020 military standoff and referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks following the deadly Galwan Valley clash.
Khera claimed the Prime Minister’s assertion that no one had entered Indian territory had weakened India’s position and created the impression that Chinese troops had not crossed the border.
The Congress leader also accused the government of conceding ground in Ladakh and questioned its response to developments in Arunachal Pradesh.
The criticism came amid renewed tensions over territorial claims in the northeastern state.
India recently rejected China’s objection to New Delhi formally identifying 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names.

stories.headline: Assam Premier League seeks to build stronger regional cricket ecosystem
stories.title: Assam Premier League seeks to build stronger regional cricket ecosystem
stories.summary: Guwahati, Aug 24 : The Assam Premier League (APL) on Sunday concluded its inaugural edition with Barpeta Braves being crowned champions after a five-wicket victory over Guwahati Royals in the Final on Sunday, bringing the tournament, to a close following a season that saw several impressive performances from both established and emerging players. The inaugural edition also emerged as a strong launchpad for emerging talent. Denish Das earned a place in the Duleep Trophy squad, signing off his stint with the Assam Premier League with a century just before leaving. Rohit Sen, Bastab Roy, Shubham Kumar Gupta and Ayushman Malakar also impressed through the tournament, underlining the next generation of cricketing talent emerging from the state, while 150 players across eight teams from Assam used the platform to make an impression. The league attracted significant attention from the wider cricketing ecosystem, with scouts from IPL franchises Kolkata Knight Riders and Royal Challengers Bengaluru present at every match. Mithun Manhas, BCCI president, was also in attendance, further highlighting the growing interest in the talent emerging from Assam. The inaugural edition delivered high-quality, competitive cricket, with multiple 200-plus scores, successful chases and thrilling last-over finishes. The Final drew more than 25,000 spectators, underlining the league’s strong connect with cricket fans across Assam. Commenting on the tournament, Taranga Gogoi, president, Assam Cricket Association said, “The Assam Premier League is an important platform for the development of cricket in Assam. The performances we have seen this season demonstrate the talent that exists across the state. Providing players with regular competitive opportunities is essential for their development, and we hope this league continues to contribute to the growth of Assam cricket. The league’s success also reflects the increasing importance of state-level competitions in Indian cricket, particularly as talent continues to emerge from markets beyond the country’s traditional cricketing centres.” The APL’s impact extended beyond the stadium, generating more than 100 million organic social media views during the tournament. This reach was achieved without media spends, influencer campaigns or reliance on players with large social media followings, reflecting the genuine interest generated by the league and its local connection. The inaugural edition also made a strong start from a commercial perspective, with 14 sponsors and partners across categories. The breadth of the partner portfolio provides an encouraging foundation for the league’s commercial growth and reflects early confidence in the property. --IANS
